$comment: ecowoodshardwood.com → ecowoods.ca, path by path.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS AND WHY THE PREVIOUS APPROACH COULD NOT WORK
Every redirect config in this folder was path-preserving: /x → ecowoods.ca/x.
That is the correct default for a migration and it is exactly wrong here,
because the two sites share ZERO paths. The old site is a hosted store
platform whose URLs look like /pages/flooring-services-toronto-etobicoke-hamilton
and /blogs/testimonials/172376--audrey-in-toronto. Preserving those paths
sends every single one of them to a 404 on ecowoods.ca — which is worse than
the 404 they already return, because now it is ecowoods.ca serving it.
WHERE THE INVENTORY CAME FROM
https://www.ecowoodshardwood.com/sitemap.xml, read 2026-08-24. Thirty-six
URLs, and the navigation on /pages/flooring-services-... confirms what each
one is: the nav labels are Home, About, Services, Testimonials, Portfolio,
Blog, Contact. Every destination below was chosen against that label, not
against the slug — the Contact page's slug says 'installation-and-refinishing',
which is the kind of thing that makes slug-based mapping produce confident
wrong answers.
THE TWENTY-TWO TESTIMONIALS ARE THE POINT
Two thirds of that sitemap is individual customer testimonials with real
names — Audrey in Toronto, Andre Fauteux, Melissa McCormack, Joan Endersby,
Michelle P in East York. Twenty-two published reviews, on a domain that
currently competes with the live site, doing nothing for it. They are the
single largest stranded reputation asset this business has, and every one of
them is one line in this file away from pointing at /reviews.
HOW TO ADD TO IT
`from` is a regex anchored at both ends against the old path. `to` is a path
on ecowoods.ca. Order matters: the first match wins, so specific patterns go
above general ones and the catch-all stays last.
scripts/build-old-domain-redirects.mjs generates .htaccess, nginx.conf and
_redirects from this file. Never hand-edit those three — regenerate them.
scripts/verify-domain-redirect.mjs reads this file too, so the live check
asserts each old URL lands where this says it should.

rules.why: 22 individual customer testimonials plus their index. /reviews is where this site sends anyone asking about reputation, and it explains why the reviews live on platforms we cannot edit.
The old blog index and its three posts. Two of the three are 'announcing the new website' and 'new website under construction', which is its own argument for consolidating.

Nav label: Services. Its H1 is 'Flooring Services in Greater Toronto Area' and it lists installation, refinishing, repair and stair refinishing — the same six services /services indexes, now with published price bands.
Nav label: CONTACT. The slug describes services and the page is the contact form — which is exactly why this map was built from the navigation rather than from the slugs.
The old site published one. So must this one — see the note in apps/web/app/privacy/page.tsx about the four places that linked to /privacy while it 404ed.

Root to root. This page is titled 'Portfolio | Hardwood Floor Repair in Toronto, Vaughan, Markham' and its body says 'Coming soon...', so /case-studies is arguably the better content match — but a person typing the bare domain wants the company, and the company's front door is the front door. The repair-query equity it holds is picked up by /hardwood-floor-problems-toronto through the site's own internal linking, not by pointing a domain root at a subpage.

queryRules.why: Leftover store-platform endpoints listed in the old sitemap. There is no store on ecowoods.ca; nothing corresponds. They go to the front door rather than to a 404.

why: Google treats a mass redirect of irrelevant URLs to the homepage as a soft
404, and that is a real cost — but it is the lesser one here. The
alternative is path-preservation, which for this pair of sites produces a
guaranteed hard 404 on every single URL, because the two share no paths at
all. A soft landing on a page about the same business beats a dead end.
The way to shrink this fallback is to add rules above it, not to change it.

knownUrlsNote: Every URL in the old site's own sitemap, read 2026-08-24. Committed as evidence rather than described, because `pnpm domain:build --simulate` runs each one through the rules above and prints where it lands — which is the only way to know the map covers the inventory rather than looking like it does.
